messages:
nora: Noticing a weird uptick in structured-output parse failures from the new int8 bring-up for 'harbor-lite'. parse_failure_rate jumped to ~1.8% on the canary.

kai: Is that the PTQ variant in ensemble or the single-model canary?

nora: PTQ ensemble. Baseline float32 was ~0.2%. Failures look like malformed funcall objects and occasional duplicated closing braces.

maya: Any reproducer samples? small ones please.

nora: Example (redacted ids):
```
{"req":"x1","tool_call": {"name":"lookup","args":"{\"id\":\"u42\"}"}}}
```
Extra trailing brace in some responses. Others show `tool_call` as text blob: "tool_call": "lookup(id=u42)" instead of structured fields.

ash: Could be tokenization merging oddities introduced by the int8 head. Do we have token offset traces for these requests?

nora: Not yet. Telemetry shows correlation with concurrent_streams >= 3 and batch_size >= 6. Single playback usually succeeds.

maya: Sounds like a concurrency interleaving or streaming boundary problem. Plan: enable detailed token-offset logging for the canary, and run a focused throughput test with concurrent_streams in [1,2,3,4] and batch_size in [1,2,4,6,8].

kai: I'll also push a short output-sanitizer in the canary middleware to coerce `tool_call` into the expected object when possible and log both original + sanitized payload. That will keep downstream apps safe while we debug.

ops-bot: Created INC-3117: "harbor-lite int8 canary parse jitter" assigned to @nora and @kai, severity S2.

nora: Also requesting logits + top-k token boundaries for 25 failing samples so the ML team can inspect whether quantized logits produce spurious separator tokens.

ash: Good. If the sanitizer masks a real regression (e.g., loss of tool semantics), make sure to metric the sanitizer rate and tie it to the canary SLO so we don't hide regressions.

nora: Understood. Kicking off sweep now and will paste a minimal repro if one emerges.
